title: A stroke, and the setup
goal: The generator's stroke (24 bits including the spelling bit), the data sources behind every pronunciation, and the IPA fallback for words CMUdict lacks.

blocks.x: A stroke is one u32
`src/generate/` gives every word a stroke. Candidate generation, cost, solver and phrase merges all work on one bit pattern per stroke; the bits are the keys.

blocks.x: The first five regions are the 22 physical steno keys; `+` and `~` are lyk's markers, tested like any bit. A stroke with only `+` or only `~` set is not a stroke.
Onset and coda consonants are different bits even for the same letter: right-bank `T` (coda t) and left-bank `T` (onset t) never collide.
Worked bit example
[[cat|KAT]] is K (left bank) + A (left vowel) + T (right bank): three of 24 bits set.

blocks.x: Setup: six sources loaded in parallel
`Setup::load` (`src/analysis/mod.rs`) loads six independent sources on separate threads (about half a second), then merges the pronunciation sources by strict priority, not as a union.

head: Source
File under `data/`
Role
rows: Word counts and rank. Names count a tenth (below).

Briefs kept as candidates (all for the 550 commonest words; beyond that only those that key the first onset or save a stroke: [faithful outlines](#/ref/collisions)); which words are written only capitalized (names).

Fifteen more dictionaries (Stan's, Josiah's, StenEd, StarTran, Tri-C and others), merged into one outline list per word (`Gold::extra`). Candidate only if it saves a stroke: [other theories' briefs](#/ref/collisions).
Word-pair counts for phrase merging, kept for ranked words only.

blocks.x: CMUdict first. A translated MFA or WikiPron pronunciation is used only where CMUdict has no entry; a CMUdict word is never touched.
Contractions spelled without an apostrophe

The frequency list counts some contractions apostrophe-stripped (`dont`, `cant`, `didnt`). If CMUdict has the apostrophe form and the list lacks it, the apostrophe form is inserted directly after the stripped one with the same count.
Names count a tenth

A word Plover and Lapwing only ever write capitalized is a name; its count is divided by ten, rounded up (435 of the 5,000 commonest words in the current build). A name never outranks its sound-alike: [[mat|PHAT]] holds `PHAT`; the name Matt types as its sound-alike after the capitalize stroke `KPA` (see [Phrases and capitals](#/ref/punctuation)).
The IPA fallback in four steps

MFA and WikiPron use IPA, in two different conventions. `src/ipa.rs` translates either into CMUdict's 39-symbol ARPAbet. About 8,000 words with no CMUdict entry are rescued this way in the current build.

head: Step
What it does
rows: Strip non-distinctive modifiers: aspiration `ʰ`, palatalization `ʲ`, length `ː`, tie bars. A syllabic-consonant mark is flagged separately and expands into an inserted schwa.
WikiPron splits a diphthong across two vowel tokens (`b a ʊ t` for bout); MFA writes one (`!aw`). Both become a single phone before lookup.
Each remaining token goes through a consonant, vowel or diphthong table. One unrecognized symbol fails the whole pronunciation; no partial translation.
Neither source marks stress. First vowel primary (`1`), every other vowel unstressed (`0`); often wrong for later-stressed words such as began.

blocks.x: Step 4 is a known limitation: stress is guessed from position, so later-stressed words can be syllabified wrongly. A word with no pronunciation gets no rule outline; it can still be spelled letter by letter (see [Spelling mode](#/ref/spelling-mode)).
